text:
Incident Bot: :rotating_light: SEV2 declared by @Rafael Mendes
Impact: p95 latency spike + elevated timeouts on Hosted API (beta ramp cohort)
Start: 1740954201
Primary: @Rafael Mendes
War room: #incidents (this thread)
Runbook: https://runbooks.redwood.ai/incidents/latency-spike

Rafael Mendes: Seeing a sharp p95 jump in us-east-1 for chat/completions starting ~2–3 min ago. Error rate creeping too (timeouts). Correlates w/ batching tier flag ramp we did ~10 min ago.
Dashboard: https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/hosted-latency/hosted-latency?var-region=us-east-1

Rafael Mendes: Quick stats last 5m (chat route): p50 +15ms, p95 +420ms, p99 +1.3s. Timeout rate up from ~0.2% -> 1.8%. Queue delay histogram shifted right.

Nadia Rahman: Confirming from metering pipeline: request volume steady, no billing anomalies. Most impacted is model `rw-llama-3.1-70b` (hosted). Token throughput stable-ish but cancellations/timeout counters increased.

Logan Wright: Telemetry view shows `queue_delay_ms` p95 went from ~18ms to ~140ms on affected pool. `batch_size` distribution shifted upward (more 12–16) and `batch_wait_ms` increased.
Link: https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/tiered-batching/tiered-batching-overview?var-tier=cost_efficient&var-region=us-east-1

Sofia Ivanova: What was the exact ramp? Was that cost-efficient tier only, or standard too? And is it applied to streaming routes?

Benji Okafor: Flag event log: `batching_tier_defaults_beta` increased from 10% -> 25% for us-east-1, model family llama-3.1, routes: chat+completions (including streaming). Change at ~1740953600.

Julian Moore: I’m looking at traces. Tail requests have long time in “scheduler_queue_wait”. No obvious kernel stalls. GPU util actually went up (from ~62% -> ~78%) but latency SLOs are getting hit.

Sean Gallagher: SLO burn is bad for fast tier customers in that region if we’re mixing traffic. Even if only beta cohort, we’re seeing spillover because pool is shared. Recommend immediate mitigation: drop flag back to 10% or lower.

Rafael Mendes: Agree. Action: rolling back flag to 5% now.
@Benji Okafor can you execute?

Benji Okafor: On it. Setting `batching_tier_defaults_beta` us-east-1 llama-3.1 -> 5% (effective in ~60s).

Incident Bot: Change recorded: feature_flag_update
Actor: Benji Okafor
Flag: batching_tier_defaults_beta
Scope: hosted/us-east-1/llama-3.1
Old: 25%
New: 5%
Time: 1740954638

Chloe Martin: Console is showing increased “time to first token” complaints from internal dogfood users too. If streaming is included, that’s probably why the perception is worse.

Sofia Ivanova: Yeah, cost-efficient tier increases queue delay tolerance + prioritizes throughput. If streaming got included, token cadence can degrade even if overall throughput is better.
Can we exclude streaming endpoints from the ramp while we debug?

Rafael Mendes: Yes. Let’s get us stable first, then decide. Watching dashboards.

Logan Wright: Early signal: queue delay p95 already trending down after rollback (from ~140ms -> ~85ms). Timeout rate still elevated but dropping.

Julian Moore: One more datapoint: saturation events from overload protection are *not* firing (load-shed counters flat). So we’re not shedding; we’re just waiting longer. That points to queue delay setting being too permissive for real traffic mix.

Sean Gallagher: If this is shared capacity, “beta cohort” can still harm others via increased queueing. Recommend temporarily disabling cost-efficient tier for streaming globally (or at least us-east-1) until we have a safe guardrail.

Connor O'Brien: FYI we’re ~2 days from runtime-1.21 branch cut. If we need a hotfix/default change, we need a decision today for what goes in vs stays behind flag.

Benji Okafor: Flag rollback to 5% is live. I can also add an exclusion rule for `streaming=true` in the rollout selector if we want. That’s a config-only change (no deploy).

Rafael Mendes: Make that change: exclude streaming for cost-efficient tier ramp in us-east-1 (keep streaming on standard tier behavior). Let’s do it now.

Benji Okafor: Applying rule: if route is chat/completions AND streaming=true -> force tier=standard (regardless of cohort). Scope: us-east-1 llama-3.1 family.

Incident Bot: Change recorded: feature_flag_rule_update
Actor: Benji Okafor
Flag/Policy: tier_selector_override
Scope: hosted/us-east-1/llama-3.1
Rule: streaming=true => batching_tier=standard
Time: 1740955222

Nadia Rahman: Timeout rate now: 0.6% and falling. p95 latency down ~250ms from peak; still slightly above baseline.

Logan Wright: Confirmed: `queue_delay_ms` p95 now ~35ms. `batch_size` distribution normalized (more 4–8). GPU util dropped back to ~66%.

Sofia Ivanova: So likely root cause: cost-efficient tier on streaming routes + real prompt-length mix leads to too many requests waiting to form larger batches. For streaming, the user feels it immediately (TTFT + cadence).
We should consider tightening `max_queue_delay_ms` guardrail when `streaming=true` even if tier=cost_efficient is selected.

Sean Gallagher: For incident closure, propose:
1) keep flag at 0% (or 5% max) until we have a revised policy
2) keep streaming exclusion in place
3) add alert for queue_delay p95 crossing threshold during ramp

Rafael Mendes: Agree. Let’s pause the ramp entirely (set to 0%) for us-east-1 llama-3.1. We can re-attempt after Sofia team adjusts guardrails + perf canary validates.
@Benji Okafor please set to 0%.

Benji Okafor: Setting ramp to 0% now.

Incident Bot: Change recorded: feature_flag_update
Actor: Benji Okafor
Flag: batching_tier_defaults_beta
Scope: hosted/us-east-1/llama-3.1
Old: 5%
New: 0%
Time: 1740955710

Chloe Martin: Noted for customer-facing comms: no external announcement needed since this was beta cohort + internal ramp, but Support may see a couple tickets from the cohort. I’ll ping CS.

Julian Moore: I’ll drop a short summary + graphs in the incident doc. Also: we should add a canary check specifically for TTFT + token cadence for streaming when tier defaults change.

Connor O'Brien: Please capture: decision is “pause rollout” + criteria to resume. Otherwise release train will keep asking.

Rafael Mendes: Incident status: stabilizing. Metrics back within normal bands.
Resume criteria draft:
- perf canary passes with streaming workloads (TTFT p95 regression <10%)
- queue_delay p95 stays <50ms at 10% cohort for 30m
- timeout rate <0.3% sustained

Sean Gallagher: :thumbsup: Works. Also add auto-rollback trigger: timeout rate >0.75% for 5m OR queue_delay p95 >100ms for 5m during ramp.

Nadia Rahman: Confirmed current: timeouts 0.22%, p95 within +40ms of baseline. No elevated cancels.

Rafael Mendes: Calling it mitigated. Keeping SEV2 until we finish postmortem notes.
Action items (creating tickets after this):
- Add streaming-specific guardrail (Sofia/Runtime)
- Add ramp alerts/auto-rollback thresholds (SRE)
- Update rollout checklist: explicitly exclude streaming for cost-efficient until proven (Release)

Incident Bot: :white_check_mark: SEV2 downgraded to Monitoring
Owner: Rafael Mendes
Time: 1740958427

Rafael Mendes: Postmortem writeup will be in the usual template. Quick TL;DR: latency spike caused by cost-efficient tier ramp including streaming traffic; increased queue delay to form larger batches drove tail latency/timeouts; mitigated by rollback to 0% + streaming exclusion + monitoring. Will follow up with guardrails + canary coverage.
